subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, including existing persisted omitted jobs, or should recurring delete-after-run remain invalid and one-shot-only?
rationale: The linked bug and this PR favor automatic recurring isolated cleanup, while the competing open PR encodes the opposite public cron contract; automation cannot safely choose that compatibility direction.

options.title: Complete recurring cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add a persisted-row, load, migration, or doctor path for existing omitted isolated jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only contract
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its caller, recovery, and docs gaps are resolved.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the new create default while explicitly documenting that existing omitted jobs need operator action or separate migration work.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add a persisted-row, load, migration, or doctor path for existing omitted isolated jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans cron store compatibility, public default semantics, and product-level lifecycle behavior, and steipete has relevant history around the one-shot default and cron normalization boundary.
